# Series 1

### b

## Exercise 1.2




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
hstart <- read.table("/home/nils/dev/mscids-notes/fs26/rtp/data/hstart.dat")

ts.hstart <- ts(
  data=hstart,
  start=1966,
  end=1974
  )

plot(ts.hstart)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-1-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::




The process is not stationary. We see a seasonal trend from 1967 to 1972.

## Exxercise 1.3

### a




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(1)

Et <- ts(rnorm(101, 0, 1))
Et[1] <- 0
y1 <- 0 #delete later

for (i in 2:length(Et)) {
y1[i] <- Et[i] - 0.5 * Et[i-1]
}

y1 = y1[2:length(y1)]
ts.y1 = ts(y1)
plot(y1, type="l")
abline(h=mean(y1), col="red")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-2-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::




The process seems stationary.

y2 = y2[2:length(y2)]

# Series 2

## Exercise 2.1

### a




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
t <- seq(1, 100, length = 100)
data <- 0.5 * t + 1 + runif(100, -1, 1)
ts <- ts(data)

plot(ts)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
print(length(ts))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 100
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(diff(ts))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-2.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
print(length(diff(ts)))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 99
```


:::
:::




We can remove the linear trend with one time backward differencing. The length of the ts increases by 1.

### b




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
t <- seq(1, 100, length = 100)
data <- 2 * t**2 + 3 * t - 1 + runif(100, -200, 200)
ts <- ts(data)

plot(ts)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-1.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
print(length(ts))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 100
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(diff(ts))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-2.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
print(length(diff(ts)))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 99
```


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
plot(diff(ts, difference=2))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-7-3.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
print(length(diff(ts, difference=2)))
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout}

```
[1] 98
```


:::
:::




We can remove the linear trend with two times backward differencing. The length of the ts increases by 2.

# Series 3

## Exercise 3.1

A -> 1
B -> 3
C -> 2
D -> 4

## Exercise 3.2

### a




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
cbe <- read.table("/home/nils/dev/mscids-notes/fs26/rtp/data/cbe.dat", header=TRUE)

ts <- ts(
  data=cbe$elec,
  start=c(1958, 1),
  end=c(1990, 12),
  frequency=12
)

plot(ts)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-12-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::




It is not meaningful to interpret the correlogram of this time series because the process is not stationary.

### b




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
decomp <- decompose(ts, type = "multiplicative")
acf(decomp$random, na.action = na.pass)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-13-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::




### c




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
elec.stl1 <- stl(log(ts), s.window="periodic")
plot(elec.stl1)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-1.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
elec.stl2 <- stl(log(ts), s.window=13)
plot(elec.stl2)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-14-2.png){width=672}
:::
:::




By simply log-transforming the data does make the process stationary.

# Series 5

## Exercise 5.1

### a




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
data <- arima.sim(list(ar = c(0.9, -0.5)), n = 100)
plot(data)
```

![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-23-1.png){width=672}
:::
:::




#### II




::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
## Theoretical autocorrelations for X_t = 0.9
## X_t-1 - 0.5 X_t-2 + e_t
plot(0:30, ARMAacf(ar = c(0.9, -0.5), lag.max = 30), type = "h", ylab = "ACF")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-24-1.png){width=672}
:::

```{.r .cell-code}
## Theoretical partial autocorrelations
plot(1:30, ARMAacf(ar = c(0.9, -0.5), lag.max = 30, pacf = TRUE), type = "h", ylab = "PACF")
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](rtp_exercises_rep_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-24-2.png){width=672}
:::
:::

## Exercise 8.1

### a

```r

```

´Error in arima.sim(model = list(order = c(2, 1, 2), ar = c(0.5, 0.5),: 'ar' part of model is not stationary´

### b

1. **Substitute the given coefficients**:
   $$
   (1 - 0.5B - 0.5B^2)(1 - B) X_t = (1 - 0.4B + 0.3B^2) E_t
   $$

2. **Expand the left-hand side (AR polynomial multiplied by the difference operator)**:
   $$
   (1 - B - 0.5B + 0.5B^2 - 0.5B^2 + 0.5B^3) X_t = (1 - 0.4B + 0.3B^2) E_t
   $$

3. **Simplify the expression**:
   $$
   (1 - 1.5B + 0.5B^3) X_t = (1 - 0.4B + 0.3B^2) E_t
   $$

The resulting expression represents an **$\text{ARMA}(3,2)$** process with the following parameters:

* **Autoregressive (AR) Coefficients:**
  * $\alpha_1^* = 1.5$
  * $\alpha_2^* = 0$
  * $\alpha_3^* = -0.5$
* **Moving Average (MA) Coefficients:**
  * $\beta_1 = -0.4$
  * $\beta_2 = 0.3$
